$comment: WHAT LEVEL AM I. Built 2026-08-22, from his own question: 'there have to be reference or
benchmarks on timings for specific levels. I want to know on what level I am with my current
timings.'
EVERY NUMBER IN HERE IS EITHER SOURCED OR MARKED CONSTRUCTED. He said in advance that real
references would only exist at the elite end and that we would have to build the rest. That is
exactly what happened, so `provenance` is on every tier and the page renders it. A tier that
says 'constructed' next to a tier that says 'sourced' is the whole reason the sourced ones can
be trusted.
COURSE AND AGE ARE NOT DECORATION. All of this is men, 35-39 (born 1991-01-24), SHORT COURSE
25 m, freestyle. His pool is 25 m and every reference here is the same course except where a
row says otherwise. An early draft of this work used the men's 50 m free world record of 20.88,
which is the LONG course record; the short course record is 19.90. Mixing the two would have
shifted every tier boundary by about 5%, which is more than the gap between two of them.
WHY THERE IS NO 25 m OR 50 m ROW. Samsung records no personal best under 100 m, and deriving
one from individual lengths does not survive the data: the fastest recorded 25 m length is
9.03 s, faster than a world-record 25 m split, and filtering the sensor miscounts moves the
answer from 14.42 s to 18.55 s depending on where the threshold goes. A number that swings four
seconds on a threshold an agent picked is not a personal best. The app asks him to swim a timed
one instead.
WHY THERE IS NOTHING ABOVE 1500 m. He swims 2 km, 3 km and 5 km, and competitive swimming does
not race those in a pool, so no tier table exists for them at any level. Those distances are
endurance facts about him, not ranked performances, and the page says so rather than inventing
a standard.

meta.courseNote: Short course, 25 m pool. The same pool he swims in.

sources.label: World records, short course 25 m
sources.note: Fetched as one consistent table on 2026-08-22 rather than assembled from separate searches, which is how the long-course 50 m record nearly got used by mistake.

sources.label: Masters world records, SCM, as of 2025-09-02
sources.note: World Aquatics. Age group 35-39 read directly out of the PDF.

sources.label: US Masters Swimming Top 10, 2025, SCM, men 35-39
sources.note: The 10th-place time is a real person who swam it this year in his age group, which makes it a far better anchor than a record nobody will approach.

sources.label: US Masters national qualifying times, men 35-39
sources.note: LONG COURSE, 50 m pool. USMS publishes no short-course-metres qualifying standard. Shown for scale and labelled, never compared like for like.

tiers.name: World class
tiers.what: The fastest man aged 35 to 39 on record, anywhere.

tiers.name: National
tiers.what: Tenth fastest in the United States in 2025, in this age group. A real swimmer, this year.

tiers.name: Qualifier
tiers.what: Fast enough to enter the US Masters national championships. Long course, so read it as a scale marker rather than a target in your pool.

tiers.name: Club
tiers.what: Comfortably inside a masters club session without being at the front of it. Set at 1.25x the qualifying time, which is a choice, not a finding.

tiers.name: Recreational
tiers.what: Swims regularly, is not training to race. Set at 1.6x the qualifying time. This is where you are.

tiers.name: Beginner
tiers.what: Can cover the distance without stopping, at whatever pace. This tier is deliberately not a time: at this stage the only question that matters is whether you get to the other end.

profileNote: His four bests score 113, 137, 154 and 130 against the age-matched world record at 100, 200,
400 and 1500. That is an unusually EVEN profile, and it tilts towards distance: he is
relatively strongest at 400 m and relatively weakest at 100 m.
The stroke data says the same thing from the other side. He takes about 9 stroke cycles per
25 m at roughly 18 cycles a minute, which is a long, slow, glide-heavy stroke. That is an engine
ahead of a technique, and it means the fastest available improvement is turnover, not fitness.
